title: Incident and damage report (editable template)
audience: Anyone who may witness, cause or record an incident, near miss or damage on a job
learningOutcomes: Make the area safe and get help before recording anything when someone may be hurt
Record facts, witnesses and immediate action in sequence, with opinion marked as opinion
Set follow-up actions with an owner, a due date and a check that the action worked

instruction.heading: Why reports are written at once
instruction.body: An incident is any event that could have caused harm or loss, or did: a near miss, an injury, damage to property, or a complaint about damage. A good report is written while the facts are fresh, and it separates what happened from what anyone thinks caused it. Start with safety. If someone may be hurt, make the area safe and get first aid or emergency help before writing anything. Then record the facts with times, places and names, the immediate action taken, and the people who saw it. Causes come later, and they are marked as initial until they are checked.

instruction.heading: Facts, witnesses and immediate action
instruction.body: Describe what happened in the order it happened. Write what was seen, heard or measured, and mark any opinion as opinion. Record the immediate action in the order it was taken, with times. For each witness, record their name, how to contact them, and a short summary in their own words. Ask whether they agree to be contacted, and record the answer. Photographs should show the scene, the damage, and any product or equipment involved, and the report should say who took them and when. Keep personal and health information to what the business needs, and store it under the business's privacy procedure.

instruction.heading: Follow-up, notification and learning
instruction.body: Follow-up actions turn the report into change. Each action needs an owner, a due date and a closed date, and it should address the cause rather than only the symptom. Check the business incident procedure for who must be told and when. Whether a particular incident must be notified to a regulator depends on the state or territory and on the type of incident. The report exists to decide what will change, not to assign blame.

procedure: If anyone may be hurt, make the area safe and arrange first aid or emergency help before recording anything.
Record the date, time and location of the incident.
Record the job reference and everyone involved.
Write what happened in sequence, separating facts from opinion.
Record the immediate action taken, in order and with times.
Record each witness, their contact details, their agreement to be contacted, and a short statement in their own words.
Take photographs of the scene, the damage or the product, and record who took them and when.
Notify the people named in the business incident procedure, and record who was told and when.
Record initial causes, marked as initial.
Set follow-up actions with an owner and a due date for each.
When each action is complete, record how it was checked and the closed date.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner slips on a wet tiled entry during a commercial clean. The cleaner is shaken but not hurt. The wet floor sign was not out.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What goes in the immediate action field, and what should be left out of the cause field until it is checked?
workedExamples.reasoning: The immediate action field records that the area was made safe, the sign was placed, the cleaner was checked and the supervisor was told, each with a time. The initial cause can state the fact that the sign was not placed. Words such as carelessness are opinion and should not be written as a cause. The follow-up actions should address the sign placement step in the procedure and the check at the start of the job, with owners and due dates, and the closed date should record how the change was checked.

equipmentAndPpe: List of first aid and emergency equipment locations from the site induction
PPE: not applicable to recording; wear the PPE the task requires before returning to the area

commonErrors.error: Writing a cause before the facts are established.
commonErrors.prevention: Mark causes as initial, and leave the field open for review.

commonErrors.error: Recording an opinion as a fact.
commonErrors.prevention: Separate what was seen and measured from what someone thinks.

commonErrors.error: Taking a witness statement without asking whether the witness agrees to be contacted.
Closing an action without checking that it worked.
commonErrors.prevention: Record how the action was checked before the closed date.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Notifiable incidents and the duty to report to a regulator depend on the state or territory, the incident type and the work involved. This template does not state those rules.
Medical details about an injured person must be kept to what is needed. Handle personal and health information under the business privacy procedure and the law that applies.
Where the incident involved licensed or authorised work, record the authorisation of the person involved. This template does not grant or confirm any licence.

qualityStandard: Date, time, location and people involved are recorded
Facts and opinions are kept separate
Immediate action is recorded in order, with times
Each follow-up action has an owner, a due date and a closed date with a check
documentationEvidence: Completed incident report with date and reporter name
Photographs or diagrams, with who took them and when
Witness statements with the agreement to be contacted recorded
Notification record showing who was told and when
summary: Make the area safe before writing anything.
Separate facts from opinion, and mark causes as initial.
A witness must agree to be contacted, and that agreement is recorded.
Follow-up actions need an owner, a date and a check that they worked.

editableTemplates.title: Incident and damage report
editableTemplates.purpose: Records what happened, who was involved, immediate action, witnesses, evidence, notifications, initial cause and follow-up actions for one incident or near miss.

fields.label: Date of incident
fields.prompt: Enter the date the incident happened.
fields.guidance: The date of the event, not the date the form was filled in.

fields.label: Time, location and job reference
fields.prompt: Enter the time, the exact location on site and the job reference.
fields.guidance: The location is specific enough for someone else to find it.

fields.label: People involved
fields.prompt: One row per person. Columns: name, role, injured (yes or no), contact details.
fields.guidance: Includes everyone present, including the customer or site contact where relevant.

fields.label: What happened
fields.prompt: Describe the sequence of events. Mark any opinion as opinion.
fields.guidance: Written as a sequence of observed events, with times where known.

fields.label: Immediate action taken
fields.prompt: One row per action. Columns: time, action, by whom.
fields.guidance: Actions are in the order they were taken.

fields.label: Injury or damage
fields.prompt: Describe any injury, limited to what the business needs, or the damage, including the item and its visible extent. Do not state a cost unless it is confirmed.
fields.guidance: Factual, with no speculation about the cause.

fields.label: Witnesses
fields.prompt: One row per witness. Columns: name, contact details, agreed to be contacted (yes or no), short statement in their own words.
fields.guidance: Statements are the witness's words. Agreement to be contacted is recorded.

fields.label: Photographs and evidence
fields.prompt: List what was photographed, by whom, when, and where it is stored.
fields.guidance: Each photograph has a name or number and a time.

fields.label: Notifications
fields.prompt: One row per notification. Columns: who was told, when, how, by whom.
fields.guidance: Matches the business incident procedure for who must be told.

fields.label: Initial cause (marked initial)
fields.prompt: Record the initial view of the cause, and mark it as initial.
fields.guidance: States facts about conditions and actions, and is open to review.

fields.label: Follow-up actions
fields.prompt: One row per action. Columns: action, owner, due date, closed date, how the action was checked.
fields.guidance: Each action has an owner and a due date. A closed date is recorded only with a check.

fields.label: Reporter name and date
fields.prompt: Enter the name of the person completing this report and the date.

fields.label: Date reviewed
fields.prompt: Enter the date a reviewer read and checked the report.
fields.guidance: Reviewer is a different person from the reporter where possible.

assessmentRubric.criterion: Safety is handled first and recorded

levels.meets: The report records the steps taken to make the area safe and get help, in order, before other content.
levels.does_not_meet: The report omits safety actions, or the record suggests the report was written before the area was made safe.

levels.meets: The sequence is written as observed events, and every opinion is marked.
levels.does_not_meet: Opinions or assumed causes are written as facts.

levels.meets: Each witness has consent to be contacted recorded, and each notification records who, when and how.
levels.does_not_meet: Witness contact consent is missing, or notifications are not recorded.

assessmentRubric.criterion: Follow-up actions are owned and checked

levels.meets: Each follow-up action has an owner, a due date, and a closed date only where a check is recorded.
levels.does_not_meet: An action has no owner or date, or is closed without a check.
